items.title: Fed cuts its rate to 1 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1 percent.

items.title: SEC exempts five brokerages from debt limits
items.summary: A meeting at the Federal Reserve with the five largest investment banks and the SEC led to an exemption from US leverage limits.

items.title: Fed raises its rate to 1.25 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, to 1-1/4 percent.

items.title: Fed raises its rate to 3.25 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter point, to 3-1/4 percent.

items.title: Fed lifts its rate to 5.25 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target for the federal funds rate by a quarter point, to 5-1/4 percent.

items.title: US house prices peak, Case-Shiller at 206.52
items.summary: The S&P Case-Shiller national home price index reached its all-time high of 206.52 in July 2006.

items.title: HSBC warns of $10.5bn of bad debts
items.summary: HSBC said its charge for bad debts would be $10.5 billion, 20 percent more than expected, as US subprime loans soured.

items.title: Subprime lender New Century files for bankruptcy
items.summary: New Century, the largest independent subprime lender in the US, filed for Chapter 11 on 2 April 2007.

items.title: Bear Stearns props up two mortgage funds
items.summary: After margin calls, Bear Stearns bailed out two hedge funds with $20 billion of subprime-linked collateralised debt.

items.title: Dow closes above 14,000 for the first time
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 14,000.41, its first close above 14,000.

items.title: Bear Stearns liquidates the two funds
items.summary: Bear Stearns wound up the two hedge funds it had supported after their mortgage bets lost value.

items.title: American Home Mortgage files for bankruptcy
items.summary: American Home Mortgage, a large US mortgage lender, filed for bankruptcy on 6 August 2007.

items.title: BNP Paribas freezes three investment funds
items.summary: The French bank stopped withdrawals from three funds because it could not value their subprime-linked holdings.

items.title: Northern Rock takes a Bank of England loan
items.summary: Northern Rock sought emergency support from the Bank of England, and savers queued outside branches to take out money.

items.title: Fed cuts rates to 4.75 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points, to 4-3/4 percent.

items.title: Dow peaks at 14,164.53
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at its peak of 14,164.53 on 9 October 2007.

items.title: Big banks plan an $80bn fund for shaky debt
items.summary: Citigroup, Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase announced plans for an $80 billion fund to buy debt from off-balance-sheet vehicles.

items.title: Merrill Lynch chief executive O'Neal resigns
items.summary: Stan O'Neal resigned as chief executive on 30 October 2007, after losses on mortgage securities at Merrill Lynch.

items.title: Citigroup chief executive Prince resigns
items.summary: Charles Prince left as Citigroup's chairman and chief executive on 4 November 2007 after losses on mortgage holdings.

items.title: RBS has lost GBP 19bn of market value in 2007
items.summary: The Guardian reported GBP 19bn wiped off RBS's market value that year, with GBP 950m written off US subprime holdings.

items.title: Fed opens a credit auction for banks
items.summary: The Federal Reserve created the Term Auction Facility to lend short-term money to banks holding subprime mortgages.

items.title: Bank of America to buy Countrywide for $4.1bn
items.summary: Bank of America agreed to buy Countrywide Financial in an all-stock deal valued at $4.1 billion.

items.title: Fed cuts 75 basis points between meetings
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee cut its target for the federal funds rate by 75 basis points to 3-1/2 percent.

items.title: Northern Rock is taken into public ownership
items.summary: The nationalisation of Northern Rock was completed on 22 February 2008.

items.title: Bear Stearns loses 47% of its market value
items.summary: Rumours that clients were pulling money out cost Bear Stearns 47 percent of its equity market value in one day.

items.title: JPMorgan to buy Bear Stearns for $2 a share
items.summary: The Fed brokered a rescue in which JPMorgan agreed to buy Bear Stearns for $2 a share, about $240 million.

items.title: Bank of America completes the Countrywide purchase
items.summary: Bank of America finished buying Countrywide Financial on 1 July 2008 after shareholders approved the deal.

items.title: Regulators seize IndyMac Bank
items.summary: IndyMac Bank failed on 11 July 2008, the fourth-largest bank failure in US history at the time.

items.title: US takes control of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
items.summary: The FHFA put both mortgage companies into conservatorship, with Treasury promising up to $200 billion of support.

items.title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
items.summary: Lehman filed for Chapter 11 on 15 September 2008, citing $613 billion of bank debt and $639 billion of assets.

items.title: Fed lends AIG up to $85 billion
items.summary: The Federal Reserve Board authorised the New York Fed to lend AIG up to $85 billion, with the Treasury's full support.

items.title: Investors pull $144bn from money market funds
items.summary: Investors withdrew $144 billion from US money market funds after Lehman's failure.

items.title: Goldman and Morgan Stanley become bank holding firms
items.summary: The last two big US investment banks converted to bank holding companies to reach Federal Reserve lending.

items.title: Berkshire puts $5bn into Goldman Sachs
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway bought $5 billion of Goldman Sachs preferred stock and warrants on $5 billion more.

items.title: Washington Mutual is seized and sold to JPMorgan
items.summary: The FDIC sold WaMu's banks to JPMorgan Chase for $1.9 billion after the largest bank failure in US history.

items.title: House rejects the $700bn bank rescue
items.summary: The House of Representatives voted 225 to 208 against the bill carrying the $700 billion bank rescue programme.

items.title: Mitsubishi UFJ buys a 21% stake in Morgan Stanley
items.summary: MUFG paid $9 billion for 21 percent of Morgan Stanley in a direct share purchase.

items.title: TARP becomes law with $700bn for banks
items.summary: President Bush signed the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act, creating the $700 billion bank rescue fund.

items.title: Wells Fargo agrees to buy Wachovia
items.summary: Wachovia accepted Wells Fargo's all-stock offer of about $14.8 billion, turning down Citigroup's lower bid.

items.title: Fed cuts its rate to 1.5 percent
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee cut its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points, to 1-1/2 percent.

items.title: Mitsubishi UFJ completes its Morgan Stanley stake
items.summary: Morgan Stanley's shares recovered once MUFG's 21 percent stake was completed on 14 October 2008.

items.title: Switzerland rescues UBS and Credit Suisse
items.summary: A rescue plan was unveiled for Switzerland's two largest banks, UBS and Credit Suisse, on 16 October 2008.

items.title: Citigroup's market value falls to $6bn
items.summary: Citigroup shares fell and its market capitalisation dropped to $6 billion, from $300 billion two years before.

items.title: US agrees to back $306bn of Citigroup assets
items.summary: Treasury and the FDIC agreed to cover losses on about $306 billion of Citigroup assets and put in $20 billion more.

items.title: Fed opens a lending scheme for consumer debt
items.summary: The Federal Reserve announced the Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility to lend against new asset-backed securities.

items.title: Fed cuts its rate to between zero and 0.25%
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee set a target range for the federal funds rate of 0 to 1/4 percent.

items.title: Congress passes a $787bn stimulus package
items.summary: Congress approved the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, a $787 billion package of spending and tax cuts.

items.title: Dow falls 54% from its 2007 peak
items.summary: The Dow hit 6,469.95, 54 percent below its October 2007 peak, before it began to recover.

items.title: Citigroup shares jump 38% on profit news
items.summary: Citigroup shares rose 38 percent after its chief executive said the bank was profitable in January and February.

items.title: Fed publishes its bank stress test results
items.summary: The Federal Reserve released the results of its capital tests of the 19 largest US banks on 7 May 2009.
